title: Ordinary affine chart extension and sections comparison with its unit equation
statement: Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism between affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $F_S=\widetilde{(-)}\circ(S.toSpec\Gamma)^*$, where the second operation is exact restriction along the canonical spectrum chart [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Let $H=\Gamma_S$ and $J=\Gamma_T$ be ordinary module-valued global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], $E$ be extension of scalars along $g.appTop$, $R$ be scalar restriction, and $K$ be the fixed tensor pullback [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. There is a natural isomorphism $c:F_SH E\cong F_SKJ$ such that for every $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$-module $N$, the extension unit at $H(F_S(N))$ followed by $R(c_N)$ equals $H$ applied to the fixed tensor-pullback unit at $F_S(N)$. The usual direct-image/sections identification is literally the identity on sections and scalars in this equation. No flatness, nonemptiness, or finite generation hypothesis is imposed. The functor order and full unit equation are recorded verbatim in lean.statement.

proof.text: Identify Gamma_X with pushforward along X.toSpecGamma followed by moduleSpecGamma. This is identity on sections. For a global function a, its scalar action on the latter is obtained by GammaSpecIso.inv followed by X.toSpecGamma.appTop = GammaSpecIso.hom. The composite is identity, so these actions agree. Naturality on sheaf maps is reflexivity. Compose tilde.adjunction with the restriction adjunction and transport its right adjoint by this concrete sections isomorphism. Restriction along X.toSpecGamma has inverse restriction along X.isoSpec.inv, using restrictFunctorComp and the chart inverse equations. Hence the chart tilde functor is fully faithful and this transported adjunction has invertible unit.

Compose the S chart adjunction with the fixed tensor pullback/direct-image adjunction. Direct image then S-sections is definitionally T-sections followed by restriction along g.appTop. Its right adjoint therefore coincides with that of extension followed by the T chart functor. Let theta be leftAdjointUniq from extension followed by T-chart to S-chart followed by tensor pullback. Define c by the inverse S chart unit under extension, then the T chart unit under extension, then T-sections of theta. Each factor is an isomorphism. Naturality of the extension unit at the inverse S unit moves it to the front. The unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app equation then turns the remaining factors into the S chart unit followed by sections of the tensor-pullback unit. Cancel the S chart unit against its inverse. This is exactly the claimed equation, as checked by the complete Lean proof.

theorem exists_mixedAffineSections_underived_chart_model
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsAffine T] (g : T ⟶ S) :
    let F : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(S, ⊤) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) :=
      tilde.functor Γ(S, ⊤) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor S.toSpecΓ
    let H := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor S.toRingedSpace
    let J := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor T.toRingedSpace
    let E := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} g.appTop.hom
    let K : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace) := Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g
    ∃ c : F ⋙ H ⋙ E ≅ F ⋙ K ⋙ J,
      ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(S, ⊤),
        (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj g.appTop.hom).unit.app (H.obj (F.obj N)) ≫
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} g.appTop.hom).map (c.hom.app N) =
        H.map ((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction g)).unit.app
          (F.obj N))
